purpose: OsteotomyCuts is a 3D Slicer scripted module for virtual osteotomies in orthognathic and craniofacial surgical planning: the user draws osteotomy lines on a bone model, sets saw direction, blade thickness and cut depth, and the bone is split into closed, watertight segments with checks of model quality and of clearance to nerve canals and tooth roots. It targets oral and maxillofacial surgeons and planning clinicians; it is explicitly research/planning software, not a medical device.
summary: No blocking issues found. The module is a single scripted module whose only imports are Slicer-bundled (numpy, vtk, qt, slicer); scipy is imported lazily behind a guard and no pip installs, network access, telemetry or downloads exist. The one subprocess call runs local `git rev-parse` without a shell. CMake installs the module script, UI files, icon and requirements.txt; EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matches the empty build_dependencies. GPL-3.0-or-later with LICENSE, SPDX headers and a clear not-a-medical-device disclaimer. Remaining items are non-blocking: a draft CLA, a committed AI-assistant notes file, and commented-out registration of the extra test scripts.

safety.rationale: Searched OsteotomyCuts.py for pip_install, urllib/requests/socket, eval/exec, pickle, torch, os.system and shell use: none found. The only subprocess call is a local `git rev-parse --short HEAD` with a list argument and no shell (lines 4332-4334); no data leaves the machine and no files are written outside Slicer's scene handling.

environment.rationale: Module-level imports are limited to Slicer-bundled packages (numpy, qt, vtk, slicer, slicer.parameterNodeWrapper); scipy is imported lazily in importNdimage() with an ImportError guard (lines 226-232) and the solid-bone feature is disabled with a warning when it is missing (line 4398). No sys.path changes, no environment variables, no global logging silencing, no pip installs.

packaging.rationale: OsteotomyCuts/CMakeLists.txt installs OsteotomyCuts.py plus Resources/Icons/OsteotomyCuts.png, both .ui files and requirements.txt, all of which exist in the tree; the catalog entry has build_subdirectory ".", category Planning and EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matching build_dependencies []. scm_revision is the branch "main", which the index supports.

license.rationale: LICENSE is the full GPL-3.0 text and every source file carries an SPDX GPL-3.0-or-later header; README states GPL-3.0-or-later and a dual-licensing option. No third-party code or model weights are bundled (Resources/requirements.txt lists no packages), so distribution permission is clear; the CLA is a contributor agreement, not a restriction on distribution.

soundness.rationale: Standard ScriptedLoadableModule/Widget/Logic/Test split with a parameterNodeWrapper for state, observers added in setup and removed in cleanup() (lines 869-879), timers stopped on cleanup, progress callbacks and slicer.app.processEvents() for long work, and errors surfaced via message boxes/logging. I read the structure, widget lifecycle, provenance and test-runner code but not the full 7,396-line geometry implementation.

utility.rationale: README, COMPATIBILITY.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md, CITATION.cff, screenshots and a quick-start plus Le Fort I worked example are present; a first-use terms dialog gates the module, and 87 headless tests plus a benchmark and an opt-in real-model script are provided. Overlap with Slicer's single-plane cut tools is explained, and the not-a-medical-device disclaimer is prominent.

findings.title: Contributor Licence Agreement is committed as an unreviewed draft
findings.evidence: > **Draft — to be reviewed by a legal professional.**
findings.explanation: CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template require every contributor to sign this CLA, and README relies on it to keep dual licensing possible, but the document itself is marked as an unreviewed draft. This does not restrict distribution of the extension (the code is GPL-3.0-or-later with a full LICENSE), so it is not an admission blocker, but contributors are being asked to sign terms the author has not finalised.
findings.suggestion: Have the CLA reviewed and remove the draft banner before enforcing it on pull requests.

findings.title: Developer/AI-assistant notes file with local paths is committed to the public repository
findings.evidence:
- Windows 11. Project: C:\Dev\OsteotomyCuts
- 3D Slicer 5.13.0 (preview build, 2026-06-30, r34833), installed for all users
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a working-notes file for an AI coding assistant: it records the author's local Windows paths, the release workflow ("Nothing is pushed publicly, tagged or put into a pull request until the user types exactly: GO RELEASE.") and instructions such as "SAFETY_NOTE and the Help / Acknowledgement texts are the user's exact wording: do not reword them." These are instructions to the author's own tooling, not to reviewers, and I found no attempt to influence review or to conceal behaviour; the file is untrusted content that I did not act on. It is only an information-disclosure/hygiene issue.
findings.suggestion: Move CLAUDE.md out of the published repository (or into a git-ignored local file) so local paths and internal workflow notes are not shipped.

findings.title: Extra test scripts are not registered with CMake, so ctest only runs the in-file test class
findings.explanation: OsteotomyCuts/CMakeLists.txt registers the unittest subclass inside OsteotomyCuts.py (line 33) and adds the Testing subdirectory, but Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt only contains a commented-out registration referring to a non-existent ${MODULE_NAME}ModuleTest.py. Consequently run_headless_tests.py, run_benchmark.py and run_real_models.py are never installed or executed by the extension build/ctest, so the 87 tests and the benchmark quoted in RELEASE_NOTES.md are not exercised by the index's automated build.
findings.suggestion: Register the headless runner (or the test class it drives) with slicer_add_python_unittest so the extension build actually runs the tests, and drop the stale commented line.

findings.title: Whole module implemented in one 7,396-line Python file
findings.explanation: All geometry, GUI, provenance and test code lives in OsteotomyCuts.py (408 KB, 7,396 lines). This is not a defect and does not affect users, but it makes review and maintenance harder and means the test class is shipped inside the module script.
findings.suggestion: Consider splitting the pure-geometry logic into a separate module file installed by CMake, keeping the ScriptedLoadableModule classes in OsteotomyCuts.py.

findings.title: Only external process invocation is a local git query, verified benign
findings.evidence:
result = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=os.path.dirname(__file__),
                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
                        creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0))
findings.explanation: The provenance feature records the module's git commit. The call uses an argument list (no shell), a fixed command, a 5 s timeout and a working directory inside the extension, and failures are swallowed into "unknown". No user input reaches it, so there is no command-injection path; recorded here because it is the only process spawn in the module.

not_checked: The bulk of OsteotomyCuts.py (lines ~400-4300 and ~4400-5160, ~5160-7396) was not read line by line; the cutting, capping, solid-model, clearance and mirroring algorithms were only assessed through the module docstrings, CLAUDE.md's description and the test scripts.
os.remove(scenePath) at lines 5923, 6025, 6969, 7184 and 7211 was not inspected in context; I could not confirm that these paths are temporary scene files created by the tests rather than user files.
The .ui files (OsteotomyCuts.ui, Disclaimer.ui) and the binary assets (icons, screenshots, SVG logos) were not inspected for embedded content.
The extension was not built or run; no CMake configure, ctest, headless test run or Slicer load was performed, so the claimed 87 passing tests and the watertightness benchmark are unverified.
The catalog entry's scm_revision "main" was not resolved to a commit and the upstream repository was not fetched; the review is based on the file snapshot provided.
questions_for_author: Are the paths passed to os.remove() at lines 5923, 6025, 6969, 7184 and 7211 always temporary scene files created by the module's own tests, and never a user-chosen path?
Should the headless test runner be registered with slicer_add_python_unittest so the extension build runs the tests, rather than leaving Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt with only a commented-out line?
Would you consider removing CLAUDE.md (local paths and internal release workflow) from the published repository?
